title: Entry drop
initial: Both chutes read as tall halfpipes facing the camera, not descending run-ups.
correction: v2 replaces them with descending channels and short amber takeoff lips; adds a small return machine.
largest: The illustrated lips sit far from the mast; the inspected lab puts both lips 19 m from it. This image establishes sightlines and mood, not map placement.

title: Ride the chute
initial: Scrap attraction, chute kerbs and amber lip read; the route depth is compressed.
correction: No correction. Preserve the clear movement composition; use actual greybox for placement.
largest: The fabricator is a rectangular banner arch instead of a clear hoop; do not replace the authored fabricator silhouette with it.

title: Airborne window
initial: Opening beam too short and warning rings lacked charcoal separation.
correction: v2 strengthens both hazard boundaries and separates mint beam from blue core.
largest: The cage and mast align with the opening beam, obscuring its endpoint. Runtime target access and beam clearance require merged geometry.

title: Impact and whole-step progress
initial: Ball already on bank with no visible core contact; badge showed four pieces plus debris.
correction: v2 places sphere at core contact; v3 removes the extra attached quarter. Three attached pieces and one detached piece now read.
largest: Badge remains a filled quartered disc attached over the cage rather than a separate annular drop ring. Keep the whole-step pop, not this badge construction.

title: Bank into steam lift
initial: Lift was clear, but Warden was above the route and crater looked like a deep pit.
correction: v2 rejected: duplicated Warden and removed lift. v3 branches from v1, keeps lift, puts one Warden below, shallows crater and exposes upper landing.
largest: The bank still reads as a walled bridge and the lift has no convincing drawn flight arc to its upper shelf. Do not copy this terrain.

title: Shelf choice and caged promise
initial: Vault was absent and routes did not end in visible kicker lips.
correction: v2 adds slate copper vault and both amber lips while preserving fast/long composition.
largest: The east stampede ground ring is unresolved beneath the distant event arch; the long route reward read still depends on its beam.

title: Reactor five-state sheet
source: LOOP-REDESIGN §2 five states and three reads
initial: Open beam was ancient blue, recover remained open, and crater was too deep.
correction: v2 makes beam mint and recovery closed with a missing badge quarter. Threat stripes persist; crater depth remains exaggerated.
largest: The punish crater still reads deeper than a traversal-safe scorch bowl; exact threat footprint is not qualified.
panels: Closed
Thin blue seam and no beam distinguish it, but body stays brighter than the source's slate/inert read.
Telegraph
Vents glow and rings appear; static art cannot show sequential vents or edge-in fill. Inner/outer ring ratio is illustrative.
Open
Mint beam differs from blue core; beam still merges with cage/mast above. No proof of target or warning clearance.
Punish
Crater remains too deep and flame-heavy. Use shallow authored geometry with the live hazard boundary.
Recover
Dome is closed and badge has a gap, but the 0.4 s departure ease is absent from a still.

title: Five families at 30 m and 6 m
source: LOOP-REDESIGN §9 family vocabulary and prompt grammar
initial: Five silhouettes were distinct but distant row too large, and lift rings used ancient blue.
correction: v2 reduces distant props, leaves prompt space and makes travel arc rings bone.
largest: The two rows are labelled viewing-distance targets, not calibrated 30 m/6 m captures. No family glyphs are invented; the UI owner must supply the real glyphs.
panels: Travel, 30 m / 6 m
Mouth and cylinders read; shown destination rings stack locally instead of tracing a real landing arc.
Opt-in fight, 30 m / 6 m
Striped cap and event ring distinguish it; timed/cost information is deliberately left for the real prompt.
Secrets, 30 m / 6 m
Wall groove reads; cache is too exposed in the niche for a hidden reward.
Temporary ally, 30 m / 6 m
Dark curled drone and dial read; rocky housing could be mistaken for scenery at distance without the source-owned glyph.
Risk bet, 30 m / 6 m
Copper box, stripes and dial read; dial does not yet show actual odds. No odds are proposed by the illustration.

title: Three visible promises
initial: Socket was on gyro ring, cage resembled a captive, and drone dial used a glyph cutout.
correction: v2 moves socket onto attached scrap part, uses spiral hardware in cage and a plain pressure dial. Drone seam is dark.
largest: The partner socket glyph is illustrative and must be replaced by the actual part-family glyph before implementation.
panels: Evolution socket
Now on an attached chunk, but glyph and paired-offer glow have no source-owned mapping in this art.
Caged break reward
Spiral silhouette invites discovery, but its topper resembles a progress badge. Reuse rarity toppers and keep the two displays separate.
Dormant ally
Dial is clear and seam dark; the dial's ticks do not express a real scrap cost.

title: Sable class-card composition
initial: Planted anchor, taut winch line and visible fox sell stored momentum.
correction: No correction. Keep this composition target for W12, with UI outside the image.
largest: The planted pylon is wall-mounted in the art; the vault-kick and pylon launch read as one composite action rather than two distinct abilities.

title: Rivet class-card composition
initial: Sprint and gunning read, but weapon slits used ancient blue and intake was cyan.
correction: v2 makes weapon working light copper and shared collection coil mint.
largest: Heat-fin and laser-rail silhouettes are less distinct than the bulky muzzle. Keep gun function legible when W12 crops to card size.

title: Kest class-card composition
initial: Perch and starburst were clear; the three sticky charges looked like suitcases and intake glowed blue.
correction: v2 reduces charges and changes intake to mint while retaining smoke and own amber blast.
largest: Rocket jump dominates; controlled glide and smoke blink remain weak reads. W12 needs separate ability pictograms or motion, not more effects in this portrait.
